newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Delta Gold puts Golden Feather on hold.
newsitem.headline: Delta Gold puts Golden Feather on hold.

text.p: Delta Gold NL said on Wednesday it has put its planned Golden Feather gold project near Kalgoorlie in Western Australia on hold because of the weaker gold price.
Delta said a recently completed feasibility study had shown the project to be technically robust, but a decision to develop the resource was not justified at the current gold price.

"The Golden Feather project has been delayed until the gold price improves, engineering alternatives being investigated reduce the cost, or the intensified exploration now underway provides additional reserves," the company said in a statement.
The Golden Feather feasibility study defined a proven and probable reserve of 3.0 million tonnes averaging 3.05 grams per tonne of gold to produce 289,000 ounces of gold at A$500 an ounce.
Elsewhere, Delta reported record attributable production of 226,589 ounces of gold for the financial year to June 30, nearly 20 percent higher than the previous year.
Delta said both Kanowna Belle, in which it has a 50 percent interest, and Granny Smith, in which it has a 40 percent stake, posted record annual production.
Annual production at Kanowna Belle was 178,726 ounces and at Granny Smith 343,064 ounces.
The cash operating cost for the June quarter was A$240 an ounce and A$276 an ounce for the the financial year.

"Strong operating cashflow will continue in 1997/98 with increased Kanowna Belle production and another similar year of high production forecast from Granny Smith," Delta chief operating officer Terry Burgess said in a statement.
Delta shares were trading two cents firmer at A$1.82 at 10.55 a.m. (0055 GMT).
